(a) **Assignment of Absolute Configuration (R/S):**
- **(i)** Compound: 2-butanol configuration.
  - Priorities: $-\text{OH}$ (1), $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (2), $-\text{CH}_3$ (3), $-\text{H}$ (4).
  - If $-\text{H}$ is horizontal/vertical, trace $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3$. Here, configuration is **(S)**.
- **(ii)** Configuration of given stereocenter with $-\text{OH}$ at top, $-\text{CH}_3$ at right, $-\text{Cl}$ at bottom, $-\text{H}$ at left.
  - Priorities: $-\text{Cl}$ (1), $-\text{OH}$ (2), $-\text{CH}_3$ (3), $-\text{H}$ (4).
  - Tracing $1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3$ yields configuration **(R)**.
- **(iii)** 1,1'-binaphthyl or substituted biaryl derivative with steric restriction: Assigned as **(S)** (axial chirality based on sequence rules applied to substituents).

(b) **Spiro Compounds:**
Spiro compounds are bicyclic organic compounds in which two rings share a single common carbon atom (known as the spiro carbon atom). 
*Example:* Spiro[3.3]heptane or 8-azaspiro[4.5]decane.

(c) **Inductive Effect vs. Mesomeric Effect:**
| Feature | Inductive Effect ($I$-effect) | Mesomeric Effect ($M$-effect) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nature** | It is a permanent displacement of $\sigma$-electrons along a carbon chain. | It is a permanent delocalization of $\pi$-electrons or lone pairs through conjugation. |
| **Distance** | It is distance-dependent and rapidly diminishes beyond 3 carbon atoms. | It is distance-independent and operates throughout the conjugated system. |
| **Type** | Operates exclusively through $\sigma$-bonds. | Operates through $\pi$-bonds or conjugated systems. |

(d) **Circular Dichroism (CD):**
- **Definition:** CD is the differential absorption of left-circularly polarized light (LCP) and right-circularly polarized light (RCP) by optically active chiral molecules.
- **Uses:** Determination of absolute configuration of chiral molecules, study of protein and nucleic acid secondary structures (folding), and conformational analysis.
proTip: In R/S configuration, if group 4 is on a horizontal bond, reverse your final answer (if clockwise appears R, it is actually S).
